The displayed selected positions -4,-1,2,5 have occupancy bead/gap/bead/gap and bead/bead/gap/gap respectively. Replacing 2 by -1 in B_1 gives empty; replacing -1 by 2 in B_2 gives (2,1) by lambda_j=beta_j-c+j. The arrows point exactly in these directions; all other positions remain fixed.

Both moves have length 3 and remain congruent to 2 mod 3 in the charged display. u=2 and v=-1 give u-e+1=0=v+1. In component 2 with c_2=1, the uncharged runner is 2-1=1, agreeing with f-c_2-1=-2=1 mod 3. v=-1 is the largest occupied charged position on runner 2 in the initial empty second component, as step 1.2 requires.

F2 defines foot=(lambda prime_j,j,component). The whole (3) hook has foot (1,1,1), leg 0 and charged content 0. The whole (2,1) hook has foot (2,1,2), leg 1 and charged content 1+1-2=0. Both are removable rim 3-hooks with empty remainder, so every component core before/after is empty by F5; sizes change (3,0) to (0,3), conserving n=3.

With component order 1<2, every relevant multipartition prefix of lambda has at least that of mu, and the first component prefix is strictly larger. The only equal-remainder pair removes the entire first component of lambda and entire second component of mu; any unchanged empty component has no hook. The local F2 supplier sets U_a=Q_a t^(na), z=q_H t. Here Q_1=1,Q_2=q_H,n=3, giving foot residues t^3 and q_H t^6 z^(-1)=t^5. The sign is (-1)^(0+1)=-1 and t^3-t^5 is nonzero in every F(t), vanishes at t=1, and has finite positive valuation. Therefore J_lambda,mu=-nu_pi(t^3-t^5) is nonzero, exactly illustrating step 1.2.
